output.review_comment:
The core fix (splitting overlong words into `width`-sized chunks before greedy filling) correctly addresses the missing behavior described in the docstring, and it makes the visible test suite pass.

However, the diff also silently changes the greedy-fill condition from
`len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width`
to
`len(current) + 1 + len(chunk) < width`

That's an unrelated, unjustified change, and it contradicts the docstring, which explicitly says a word is appended "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long" (i.e. `<=`, not `<`). With the strict `<`, a combination that exactly fills the line to `width` characters will now be wrongly rejected and pushed to the next line — an off-by-one regression relative to the documented spec.

None of the tests in `tests/test_wrap.py` happen to exercise the exact-width-fit boundary case, so the suite passes, but this is exactly the kind of edge case the "notifications team" spec (per the docstring) cares about, and it will likely break as soon as such a case is tested (e.g. `wrap_text("ab cd", 5)` should yield `["ab cd"]` but will now yield `["ab", "cd"]`).

Please restore the `<=` comparison — the word-chunking fix alone is sufficient to satisfy both the tests and the documented contract; the `<`/`<=` swap should be reverted.
